properties.name: reflow2 keeps just about every package in Cargo.toml at or near its latest release, monitored continually, and adapts its own code to new versions rather than staying on old ones
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-10-01, dev_reflow2 hub session (/req): "as with all our packages in the Cargo.toml, we have to continue to monitor and adapt reflow2 to use the latest. We can get stuck using old code because we didn't want to adapt. If we choose this philosophy, we will fall behind. I want reflow2 to keep a cutting edge of the latest or near latest of just about every package in Cargo.toml"

WHAT PROMPTED IT: the full dependency sweep the same night (fact:dependency-audit-2026-10-01-the-full-sweep). It found the switch to the maintained rust-rocksdb crate, accepted on 2026-08-24 (dec:absorb-rocksdb-024-unchanged-then-switch-separately), never done. The workspace Cargo.toml has carried "the switch gets its own PR" since then, and the engine underneath is now a major RocksDB version behind (10.4.2 against 11.8.1). The 2026-09-13 snapshot had called the audit "not pressing" (fact:dependency-audit-snapshot-2026-09-13).

WHAT IT ASKS, as worded by the agent for Anthony to confirm:
1. MONITORED, NOT AUDITED ONCE. Every direct dependency in the workspace and crate manifests is checked against its latest release on a recurring basis, and each check is recorded with its date.
2. AT OR NEAR LATEST. Patch and minor releases inside a declared range are taken promptly with a lock refresh. A new major (or new 0.x series) is adopted by its own PR that adapts reflow2's code. "Adapting is work" is never a reason to stay behind.
3. AN EXCEPTION IS RECORDED, NEVER SILENT. A dependency held back carries a written reason and a date to look again. Real reasons exist:
   - an upstream regression;
   - a protocol revision reflow2 adopts deliberately (req:reflow2-conforms-to-the-mcp-specification-revision-it-serves says a new MCP revision is never inherited silently by a bump. That governs HOW such a bump lands, not WHETHER);
   - a platform pin made on purpose, such as the ubuntu-22.04 build runner and image base kept for glibc reach.
4. A BUMP IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. Each upgrade PR passes the full suite. Where a bump touches stored data or the release machinery, it proves that before merge: existing stores open unchanged, or a release dry run passes.

NOT YET SAID, and left open for Anthony:
- how often the monitoring runs (on a schedule, before each release cut like the hub's standards practice, or both);
- what does it (a CI job that opens PRs, a reflow2 tool, or a periodic sweep in a session);
- whether the spirit extends beyond Cargo.toml to the GitHub Actions, the Rust toolchain and the container base image, which the same sweep found behind or deliberately pinned.

2026-10-02 — THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ANSWERED BY ANTHONY: "both before release cuts and monthly, CI job, include actions too."
- WHEN: before every release cut, AND monthly.
- WHAT DOES IT: a CI job, a scheduled workflow plus a step the release cut runs. It reports every direct dependency (all Cargo.toml manifests) and every GitHub Action against its latest release, and records the dated result.
- SCOPE: the Cargo.toml packages AND the GitHub Actions the workflows use.
Not yet said: the Rust toolchain floor (rust-version), measured 2026-10-02 in fact:rust-version-1-94-was-set-once-and-nothing-checks-it-2026-10-02, and the container base image (a deliberate ubuntu:22.04 pin). Both are left to him.
